name: Cameo Green
lede: Cameo Green is a soft, light yellowish green from Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, most common in the paintings of Van Gogh, Munch and Klimt.

sections.title: A dictionary green from around 1904
sections.body:
Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary of color dates the name to about 1904, at plate 27, column B, chip 6, hex #92B99A [1]. No Ridgway or ISCC-NBS plate is recorded for it independently; the ISCC-NBS committee's 1955 match places it in block 135 among the "light yellowish green" names, 6.0 units away [1]. Its Munsell renotation is 2.0G 7.1/3.5, a pale, low-chroma green [1]. The origin of the name is undocumented here [1].

Its nearest library neighbor is [[deep-glaucous-green|Deep Glaucous-Green]], about 2.9 units away and slightly greyer [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: A color within six units of Cameo Green covers at least five per cent of the canvas in 49 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.2 per cent, as photographed [2]. It peaks in paintings from the 1910s, and Vincent van Gogh, Edvard Munch and Gustav Klimt each carry it nearly thirty times the archive average [2]. Fittingly, it also shows up far more in Norwegian and Austrian paintings than average, Munch's and Klimt's home countries [2]. Its earliest appearance is a 1480 *Flight into Egypt* by Bernardino Jacobi Butinone [2]. These are photographs of varnished paintings, read as screen colors [2].
